pr_title: config: allow setting context length through env var
pr_body:
From offline discussions:

- Current API parameters improperly mix system and request level configurations
- For now, let users set a context length through `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`
- Users can still set `num_ctx` through the CLI or SDK on a request level but is expected to be moved away from in the future

closes: #6504, #8794, #5356, #5357
pr_comments: So it doesn't close #5356, right? We won't be able to set `num_ctx` using the OpenAI API call 😞

> So it doesn't close #5356, right? We won't be able to set `num_ctx` using the OpenAI API call 😞

I think it would be good enough to close for a couple reasons:
1. You'd just be able to set an env var so it would override the default `num_ctx` that gets set
2. You also wouldn't have to worry about changing the API and this env var wouldn't interfere with any of your existing setups making the switch easier.
Looks like this is a global variable and not model specific. While this is a welcome change, I'm not sure it addresses the issue of being able to adjust context dynamically.

This does appear to be a much simpler solution to the problem of Ollama forcibly shortening the context to shorter than the model can handle. I suppose supporting the changing through the API would add flexibility, but it is unnecessary - if you're using the OpenAI API it's because you're building or using tooling that is compatible with the OpenAI API and the best solution there is to let the model [config] handle it as they would.

> Looks like this is a global variable and not model specific. While this is a welcome change, I'm not sure it addresses the issue of being able to adjust context dynamically.

Yeah completely understand. I'd defer to using the Python/JS SDKs in that case. Planning to clean up most of this anyways and figure out some better patterns for model loading/eviction, as well as setting system level parameters. Aiming for a lot of the systems level config to be dynamically configured.

As for this in particular I'd consider per-model context length a feature of our SDKs. for now...

I like this as it is externalizing a hard coded default.

This currently impacts users of tools like smolagents where they local test with ollama and use possibly something else at runtime but want to use same openai driver regardless. I personally ran into this with block/goose as well.

What would the behavior of OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=0 be? In llama.cpp, that defaults it to the trained context length, would that be the case here? Regardless of the choice, it'd be nice to have a test for whatever behavior we settle on

> What would the behavior of OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=0 be? In llama.cpp, that defaults it to the trained context length, would that be the case here? Regardless of the choice, it'd be nice to have a test for whatever behavior we settle on

My 2p is to treat 0 as a "zero value" like unset, so if this is there, use the default which is currently the hard-coded value and not model specific. That's easier to document as if our default switches to be model specific, we don't have to go back and clarify that 0 is a special value.

> > What would the behavior of OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=0 be? In llama.cpp, that defaults it to the trained context length, would that be the case here? Regardless of the choice, it'd be nice to have a test for whatever behavior we settle on
> 
> My 2p is to treat 0 as a "zero value" like unset, so if this is there, use the default which is currently the hard-coded value and not model specific. That's easier to document as if our default switches to be model specific, we don't have to go back and clarify that 0 is a special value.

Yes 0 should be treated as the current default of `2048` as we have already. Thanks for bringing this up @JackYoustra @codefromthecrypt

> I like this as it is externalizing a hard coded default.
> 
> This currently impacts users of tools like smolagents where they local test with ollama and use possibly something else at runtime but want to use same openai driver regardless. I personally ran into this with block/goose as well.

Will do this as a follow up to allow fetching the model. Currently if the value is < 4 then it will default to 4.

issue_context.title: allow for num_ctx parameter in the openai API compatibility
issue_context.body:
The OpenAI compatibility module does not allow for setting the number of tokens window (num_ctx) via API call dynamically instead of having to adjust the Modelfile each time we want to use another context window.

Therefore it would be great to have in the OpenAI compatibility. I can also try a PR for this.

Thanks a lot for this wonderful project! :-)
comments: +1 to this from me! This would be helpful.
There seems to be a pull request for that - is there any help required to merge it probably?

Unfortunately OpenAI's API doesn't have a way to do this, and we can't modify the `num_ctx` parameter directly with their API. I did write up a [doc](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/openai.md#setting-the-context-size) which explains how to accomplish this though. Hopefully this makes sense. I'll close the issue, but feel free to keep commenting.
Can we use a custom header to specify this? Having to create a modelfile makes it quite difficult for tool builders to make their tools work out of the box for end users.

review_comments: This looks great. It's nominal, but could we add a test to `types_test.go` that calls `t.Setenv("OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH", <value>)` and then compares the default options?
